chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Mu'adh al-Jawhari, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (blessings of God upon them), from the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family), from Gabriel (peace be upon him).

He said: God, Majestic is His Majesty, said: Whoever commits a sin, whether minor or major, and does not know that it is up to Me to punish him or forgive him, I will never forgive him that sin. And whoever commits a sin, whether minor or major, and knows that it is up to Me to punish him or forgive him, I will forgive him.

key_terms.أَعْفُوَ عَنْهُ: A'fu 'anhu (I forgive him): Divine pardon, an expression of God's mercy
key_terms.أُعَذِّبَهُ: U'adhdhibahu (I punish him): Divine punishment, the prerogative of God
key_terms.جَلَّ جَلَالُهُ: Jalla jalaluhu (Majestic is His Majesty): A glorification formula for God
key_terms.غَفَرْتُ: Ghafartu (I forgave): Past tense used for emphatic divine oath

ai.seo_question: What is the hadith qudsi about God's forgiveness of sins based on the sinner's knowledge?
ai.summary: This hadith qudsi (divine narration) is transmitted through a remarkable chain from Gabriel to the Prophet to the Imams. God declares that the sinner who denies God's authority over punishment and forgiveness will never be forgiven, while the sinner who acknowledges God's absolute sovereignty over pardon and punishment will receive divine forgiveness. The key theological point is that recognizing God's absolute prerogative (mashiyyah) in matters of sin and forgiveness is itself a form of proper belief that opens the door to divine mercy.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us from his father from Muhammad b. Abi `Umayr from Mu`adh al-Jamhuri from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (s) from the Messenger of Allah from Gabriel (as).

He said: Allah said: Whoever commits a minor or major sin, and he does not know that its punishment or forgiveness is up to Me, then I will never forgive him. Whoever commits a minor or major sin, and he knows that I can punish him or forgive him for it, then I will forgive him.
